title: Lagavulin vs Laphroaig
subtitle: Two Islay distilleries and the firm that sold both
description: For sixty years the firm that ran Lagavulin also sold Laphroaig's whisky. When Laphroaig ended the agency in 1907, Peter Mackie built a small distillery inside Lagavulin to make whisky like Laphroaig. Four pours.

pours.name: Craigellachie 13
pours.notes: From the Speyside distillery Peter Mackie invested in in 1890. No peat, so start here.

pours.name: White Horse
pours.notes: Mackie's blend, registered in 1890 and built on Lagavulin. Look for the Islay smoke in it.

pours.name: Lagavulin 16
pours.notes: Mackie's own distillery. Keep some back to taste beside the Laphroaig.

pours.name: Laphroaig 10
pours.notes: The whisky Mackie sold for years and then tried to copy. Same strength as the Lagavulin. Made two miles away.

tags: scotch, islay, peat, single malt, blended scotch
